features.name: Sonos GENA event subscriptions - push transport state instead of polling
features.desc: Replace poll-based transport/zone state with Sonos GENA (UPnP General Event Notification Architecture) event subscriptions. The app SUBSCRIBEs to each speaker's AVTransport and RenderingControl services; Sonos then pushes an HTTP NOTIFY to an in-app callback (via the existing in-app HTTP server, fLocalHTTPServer) the instant transport, track, or volume changes, instead of Sorriva polling every 2-5s. Benefits: near-instant updates, no poll-interval latency, far less network chatter, and it dissolves the external-change staleness window that the PlaybackStore rearchitecture otherwise mitigates with hold-last-good. Requires subscription lifecycle management: renew before timeout, re-subscribe on network change, unsubscribe on teardown. Strategic note: had GENA been known at design time, the transport layer would have been built on it from the start. Sequenced as a future tightening AFTER the PlaybackStore authoritative-declaration rearchitecture is stable and ZoneDiscoveryService is decomposed, at which point poll-to-push can be swapped behind the same transport interface without changing anything above it.

features.name: Sonos Radio track title displays as the station name
features.desc:
Sonos Radio station started in Sonos carries over album artwork in zone but track name shows up as station name. track and artist do not update in miniplayer nor Now Playing. Edge case in which Sonos radio is not a source in Sorriva.

ROOT CAUSE (2026-08-04): dc:title means something different per service. iHeart reports a filename (hls.m3u8), SomaFM a stream slug (secretagent-128-aac), and Sonos Radio the TRACK title. Sorriva treats a valid-looking dc:title as the station name, so for Sonos Radio the track lands in the station slot. Track and artist stay blank because Sonos Radio does not populate r:streamContent the way iHeart and SomaFM do, and that is where those two fields are read from.

This is exactly the ambiguity the per-service adapters in RadioServiceAdapter.swift exist to resolve, and there is no Sonos Radio adapter — Sonos Radio is not a source in Sorriva, so there are no stored stations to reverse-resolve against. Two options: (1) write a Sonos Radio adapter that knows dc:title is the track and maps the fields correctly, or (2) as a general guard, stop trusting dc:title as a station name whenever no adapter claims the URI, and surface it as track instead. Option 2 is the safer default because it also protects against the next unknown service; option 1 gives a correct station name as well. See engineering/radio-service-integration.md.

features.name: Zone discovery restart loop on uncached devices
features.desc: Discovery restart loop on any device with no cached zone topology. NWPathMonitor invokes pathUpdateHandler immediately on start(), not only on change. The monitor was created inside startDiscovery() and cancelled by stopDiscovery(), so the satisfied callback fired handleNetworkRestored() -> stopDiscovery() -> startDiscovery() -> new monitor -> callback. Approximately 400 iterations/sec; 48,374 cycles observed in 122s on first iPad launch. The NetServiceBrowser was destroyed roughly every 2.5ms, well before Bonjour could resolve any service, so zones never populated and the exit condition was never reachable. Fix: network monitor and both NotificationCenter observers moved to init as service-lifetime concerns; stopDiscovery no longer cancels the monitor; transition-into-satisfied detection added so only a real network change triggers rediscovery; 10s restart floor added as a guard against any future repeating caller. Also fixed in the same pass: both observers were re-registered on every startDiscovery() call and never removed, leaking approximately 96,700 live observers over the captured session. Browser and resolve delegate diagnostics converted from print() to sLog() so Bonjour behaviour reaches the debug export.

features.name: Network-scoped zone topology cache
features.desc: Zone topology cache keyed by IPv4 subnet rather than a single flat UserDefaults key, so a device taken to a different Sonos system restores nothing and discovers fresh. New file NetworkIdentity.swift derives the key from getifaddrs as CIDR (e.g. 192.168.1.0/24) with no entitlements and no permission prompts. Subnet keys collide across locations sharing a common private range, so the cached entry also carries the Sonos household ID from GetZoneGroupAttributes; once real topology arrives the live household is compared against the restored one and the entry is discarded and rewritten on mismatch. syncTopologyToDB now returns the live household ID and the cache write moved to after it, so the household is known at write time. The pre-existing network-agnostic key is deleted on sight and never read. Default gateway was evaluated as an additional key component and rejected: within a given subnet the gateway is almost always x.x.x.1, so it adds no entropy in the exact collision case it was intended to resolve, at the cost of a fragile routing-table walk.

features.name: Scope user-owned state to Sonos household
features.desc: Investigate scoping user-owned state to the Sonos household rather than globally, for users with more than one Sonos system (home plus a second property or a work install). Library sources, favorites, presets, and persisted zone state are currently global, so a home NAS share would appear on a system that cannot reach it. The household ID is already persisted in the households table and validated against cached topology, so the join key exists; the open questions are which entities scope per-household and whether a user-facing household name is surfaced in settings. The raw CurrentMuseHouseholdId is opaque and should stay hidden; if anything is surfaced it should be a friendly name read from GetZoneGroupAttributes and renameable by the user. Distinct from fHouseholdProfiles, which is multi-profile support within one account, not multi-system scoping.

features.name: Per-service radio adapters - each provider identifies its own stations
features.desc: Replace the single global URI-matching heuristic with one adapter per streaming service, each of which knows its provider's URI shape exactly: iHeart by station code (zc8681), SomaFM by channel slug (secretagent). RadioServiceRegistry asks the adapters to identify a stream first and falls back to generic normalisation only for URIs no adapter claims. Tom's call, and the right one: a global rule set accumulates an exception per service and every new provider re-breaks the previous ones -- 'instead of trying to make a global rule set against all radio stations we need code for each service so it is handled exactly as it needs to be'. Adding a service is now a new adapter file rather than an edit to shared matching logic. Integration guide, including what each service does and does not report, in engineering/radio-service-integration.md.

features.name: AIFF tracks scanned with no duration, so no total time when playing
features.desc: The AIFF COMM parser read the 80-bit extended sample rate at the wrong offset -- it took offset+14, which is sampleSize, not the start of the rate field. The exponent came out as 16 instead of ~16398, so 2^(16-16446) underflowed to 0.0, and a zero rate made the duration calculation fail silently: the track scanned fine and played fine, it just had no total time. Fixed by reading the exponent at offset+16 and the full 8-byte mantissa at offset+18. Confirmed on device: AIFF files now show total time.

features.name: Local track loads with artwork and metadata but never starts playing
features.desc: A zone whose transport was left in a wedged state accepted SetAVTransportURI and reported the new track -- artwork, title and artist all updated correctly -- but Play did nothing. Fixed by issuing Stop before SetAVTransportURI on both local playback paths, and by adding verifyPlaybackStarted, which reads GetTransportInfo shortly after the Play command and logs whether the zone actually entered PLAYING. Cost three wrong theories before empirical raw-SOAP testing found it (share registration, .local hostname resolution, and DIDL duration metadata were each blamed and each cleared) -- the verification step exists so the next occurrence is visible rather than inferred.

features.name: Two zones on the same station displayed different names
features.desc: Idle and playing zones had SEPARATE station-resolution implementations that disagreed. The idle one trusted Sonos's dc:title ahead of the stations table and returned early when a name was present, so it never did the lookup at all; its fallback also searched iHeart only, so a SomaFM station could not have resolved there in any case. Result: two zones parked on the same SomaFM stream, one showing the curated 'Groove Salad' and the other the raw slug 'groovesalad-128-aac'. Every fix applied to the playing path left the idle path broken. Fixed by deleting the duplicate -- both paths now call one stationDisplay(for:) resolver where the stations table wins and dc:title is only a fallback. Also fixed in the same place: the resolver discarded its own result when a zone had no context yet (the common idle case), and left the previous local album's embedded artwork in place, which the mini player prefers -- so a station could display wearing an album cover.

features.name: One failed station lookup stranded a zone until the app was force-quit
features.desc: Station lookups are cached per zone to stop them re-running on every poll, and a MISS was cached with no expiry. Since the cache is memory-only, a single failure meant the zone showed the raw stream name until the app was relaunched -- which is exactly the 'closed and relaunched and it self-healed' signature. The trigger was a second defect: a transfer briefly groups the destination to the source, during which Sonos reports its URI as x-rincon: (a speaker address, not a stream). That was being treated as a radio stream and sent to the station lookup, manufacturing a miss. Fixed both: x-rincon: is excluded from the radio-stream test alongside queue and local URIs, and a cached miss now expires after 30s. The expiry is the more valuable half -- the grouping hole is closed, but the pattern of one bad lookup poisoning a zone would have resurfaced with the next unfamiliar URI shape, looking like a different bug each time.

features.name: Radio zone stuck on the track that was playing when the station started
features.desc:
A playing radio zone keeps showing the track and artist that were current at the moment the station was declared, forever. Station name and artwork stay correct. Observed live 2026-08-04: Master Bedroom on iHeart Lost 80s, Sonos reporting Eurythmics and then Prince ~80s later, while the app displayed Chaka Khan -- a song that had played several tracks earlier.

ROOT CAUSE: the reducer's first precedence branch in PlaybackStore.resolveContent -- 'Sonos confirms what we declared, therefore authoritative; polling cannot override'. That is sound for a local file, whose URI changes with every track, so one URI really does mean one piece of content. It is false for a stream: the URI is the STATION (.../zc7934/hls.m3u8) and never changes while the songs do. So the branch matches on every poll forever and returns the snapshot frozen at declare time. Polling reports the correct track continuously and is discarded BY DESIGN.

FIX (BUILT 2026-08-04, compiles clean; left open pending field verification -- Tom is running it for several days to see whether it manifests again): branch the confirmed-URI case on content kind. A local declaration returns unchanged -- the app owns all of it because Sonos has neither the track nor the art. A stream declaration returns its station identity with the LIVE track and artist layered on, since Sonos reports those correctly via r:streamContent and the app cannot know them. Hold the previous track rather than blanking if Sonos reports empty between songs. Confined to resolveContent; the URI check still gates the branch, so a declaration still cannot display a station the zone is not playing.

WIDER POINT, worth keeping: declarations exist to cover the 1-2s gap between the app issuing a command and Sonos confirming it. They were then given permanent authority over content, which is a far bigger claim than that problem needs -- the exception became the rule, and every 'what's playing' ghost is a case where the app's copy went stale and that rule blocked reality from correcting it. Note this is NOT fixed by moving to GENA event subscriptions: push changes how the app learns of a change, not what it does with it, so the same rule would freeze content just as hard. See HANDOFF-playbackstore-design.md sections 3.1 and 12.1. BLOCKS phases C/D/E.

features.name: A stopped zone shows what Sorriva last knew, not what the speaker last played
features.desc:
For a zone that is not playing, the reducer returned the stored last-playing outright and never reached the line that returns what polling had just resolved. So every poll resolved the zone's parked URI correctly -- station against the stations table, local file against our database -- and the answer was then discarded.

WHY IT MATTERS MOST FOR EXTERNAL SOURCES: Sonos keeps reporting the URI a stopped zone is parked on, so it can always tell us what a zone last played, including content started from the Sonos app that Sorriva has no record of. Start something externally and it appears correctly WHILE PLAYING (the stopped-zone rule does not fire), then stop it and the card reverts to whatever Sorriva itself last knew for that zone -- possibly hours old and from a different source. Tom's framing: the code is supposed to poll the endpoint, find out what it is, and resolve it -- and it does; the display half was overriding the result.

ROOT CAUSE, and it is an over-correction rather than a design choice: that rule was written to stop the card reading RAW SonosZone fields such as stationName, which polling mutates and which caused the reverting-station and blanking-artwork bugs. Sound for raw fields. But it was written broadly enough to also block the RESOLVED context, which is not raw residue -- it is the URI enriched by our own database -- so the good answer was suppressed along with the bad one.

FIX: delete the early return. The existing final line already falls back to the stored copy, so a stopped zone now shows the resolved answer when there is one and the stored copy only when Sonos cannot describe the zone at all -- a speaker back from a power cut with an empty transport. That is the one job the stored copy is genuinely needed for, and it makes 'self-heals on the next poll' true for stopped zones instead of only for playing ones.

THIRD INSTANCE of one pattern: something the app stored outranking something Sonos just reported. See also bStationTrackFrozenByDeclaration and the grouping ghost fixed in fPlaybackStoreGroupDeclarations.

features.name: PlaybackStore phase C - grouping needs no declarations; Sonos restores the member
features.desc:
CLOSED WITH A NEGATIVE RESULT. The premise was wrong and the behaviour it set out to change was already correct.

PREMISE (wrong): 'an ungrouped zone reports what it played before it was grouped' was recorded as a defect, on the assumption that a separating zone keeps the group's content.

WHAT SONOS ACTUALLY DOES, verified by querying the speakers directly rather than by reading our code: a grouped member NEVER receives the stream. Its transport is set to x-rincon:RINCON_<coordinator>, a pointer at the coordinator, which does the streaming and distributes the audio. The member's own queue is untouched for the whole time it is grouped, and Sonos restores it on separation. Measured: Patio coordinating SomaFM Bossa Beyond (aac://.../bossa-128-aac) with Garage grouped to it; after ungrouping, Garage was STOPPED and parked on its own hls-radio://.../zc7934 (iHeart Lost 80s), not the group's stream. Sonos's own app shows no station for Garage yet pressing play starts Lost 80s -- Sonos does not consider the member to be playing anything, it simply has that URI in its transport.

THEREFORE the pre-existing behaviour was right: what an ungrouped zone reports is what will actually play if the user presses play on it. Tom's ruling: 'sonos ALWAYS is the source of truth.' Declaring the coordinator's content onto a member would make the card describe something the speaker will not do.

BUILT THEN REMOVED: projectCoordinatorContent(coordinatorID:onto:) and its three call sites. It was harmful in both directions -- on joining it overwrote the member's real last-playing with the coordinator's content, destroying the zone's own history that Sonos was about to restore; on leaving, its grace window asserted the group's content for a few seconds before polling contradicted it, which is the flicker that exposed the whole mistaken premise.

KEPT from this work, both worth having on their own: Stop after becomeCoordinator on each separation path, and contentDeclaration(forZoneID:) -- one resolution order (live declaration, then last-playing only while its URI still matches, then the resolved context, then raw synthesis as a last resort) with transferPlayback's three inline branches collapsed onto it. An intermediate version of that resolver put raw synthesis ahead of the resolved context and an ungrouped zone showed correct artwork beside the name 'hls.m3u8', since synthesis reads Sonos's dc:title; raw fields must never outrank resolved ones.

PROCESS NOTE worth keeping: the premise was asserted from reading code and was wrong. Three rounds of fixes were built on it, each producing a new symptom, before querying the speakers settled it in one command. Check what the hardware does before recording a behaviour as a defect.

features.name: Move Swift sources into synchronized folders so new files are picked up automatically
features.desc:
67 Swift files sit at ios/ root and are listed individually in the Xcode project (74 explicit PBXFileReference entries). Only ios/Sorriva/ and ios/SorrivaTests/ are PBXFileSystemSynchronizedRootGroup folders, and nothing lives in them. Consequence: every new source file must be added to the project by hand or the build fails -- and it fails as a missing-symbol error that points at the call site rather than at the project file, so the cause is not obvious. This bit on 2026-08-04 when RadioServiceAdapter.swift was added for the per-service radio adapters; the build failed until Tom added the file manually.

WORK: move the 67 files into the synchronized ios/Sorriva/ folder, strip their explicit references from project.pbxproj, and handle server/swift-config.json, which enumerates the file list and would go stale (regenerate or retire it). Mechanical, but it touches the project file, so it wants a clean tree and a verifying build.

SEQUENCING: Tom deliberately tabled this on 2026-08-04 until PlaybackStore phase B was tested and working -- 'let's table the restructure until phase b is tested and working' -- which it now is. His reasoning for not deferring further: 'definitely better to do it sooner than later before the project grows larger.' Phases D and E both add files, and the UI work will add many, so the cost of waiting compounds. Do it on a clean tree at a known-good point rather than mid-feature.

features.name: Station resolution re-runs on every poll for every zone instead of once per URI
features.desc:
Observed 2026-08-04 in a console filtered on CONTEXT: every zone re-resolves its station on every poll cycle, indefinitely. The same zone/station pairs repeat dozens of times -- 'resolved station from URI - Bossa Beyond for RINCON_804AF2A73E9901400' roughly 40 times in one capture, alongside Lost 80s and Yacht Rock Radio for other zones. Each line is a SUCCESSFUL resolve, so the lookup works; it simply runs again next poll.

This is what the resolvedStations cache in PlaybackContextService exists to prevent, and the same churn was reportedly fixed once before (bPlaybackContextResolveChurn -- 'forty re-resolutions of a single station in one log', which is precisely what is happening again). Each resolve reads the full stations table and re-runs adapter matching.

NOT DIAGNOSED. The cache read looks correct on inspection: stationDisplay(for:) computes normalizedStreamKey(zone.currentTrackURI), takes the cached entry only when its stored key matches, and re-resolves only on a nil entry or an expired miss. resolveStationFromURI writes the entry immediately before emitting the log line above. For the cache to miss every poll, either the entry is not landing or the key differs between write and read -- those need opposite fixes and the log cannot distinguish them. Ruled out by inspection: the normalised key strips scheme and query, and iHeart URIs measured directly off the speaker carry no query string, so token rotation is not the explanation. There is only one call site, and observe() is guarded against double registration.

IMPACT: no visible symptom today, but it is wasted network and database work every poll for every zone, and it is why a raw-name flicker was visible at all during the phase C work -- the raw dc:title fallback in stationDisplay only shows when the cache misses, so a working cache would have hidden that class of error. Next step is instrumentation: log the stored key and the computed key side by side on a cache miss.

features.name: Apple TV — home screen

features.desc: Natural language playlist generation from full music graph. Examples: 'Sunday Morning Coffee', 'Late Night Drive', 'Dinner Party'. Draws from local library and all connected streaming services. Profile-aware. Returns playlist with reasoning — explains the thread connecting choices.

features.name: Deriva — music discovery
features.desc: Analyzes most played tracks, artists, genres across all sources. 'Music just like this' from any artist or track. Gateway albums — 'if you love X, here's Y you haven't explored'. Deep cuts surfacing per artist. Sources: MusicBrainz + Last.fm similarity APIs.

features.name: Deriva — skip pattern learning
features.desc: Track skips and abandons across all sources. Learn genre, era, style avoidance patterns per profile. Stop including patterns that consistently get skipped. Improve playlist and auto-play quality over time.

features.name: Deriva — library rediscovery
features.desc: Surface forgotten and unplayed albums in library. 'You added this 3 years ago and never played it.' Cross-reference with listening patterns to find likely matches. Scheduled rediscovery suggestions.

features.name: Auto Play
features.desc: Continuous play seeded from currently playing track — the core listening loop that keeps music going beyond a single album. Tightness dial: strict (same genre/era) to open (anything goes). Pulls from local library first, streaming services second. The primary vehicle for rediscovering music you already own and the bridge into new discovery. Powered by Last.fm similar tracks API + Deriva pattern learning.

features.name: Deriva — contextual soft signals
features.desc: Time-of-day and seasonal awareness as soft signals for playlist generation. Optional weather API integration. Signals inform but don't hard-filter — AI weighs them naturally.

features.name: Listening stats reset and ignore controls
features.desc: Give users control over listening statistics: reset all stats or reset by type (tracks, albums, artists, stations, playlists). Alternatively or additionally, mark specific artists, albums, tracks, or stations as ignored — excluded from stats reporting, listening history display, and Deriva pattern learning without deleting play history. Ignore is preferable to delete for items the user no longer listens to but doesn't want skewing recommendations.

features.desc: Read Shazam library and generate playlist. Resolve each tag to local library → subscribed service → fallback. Best-effort write-back sync via Apple's limited Shazam API.

features.name: Playback statistics
features.desc: Albums, tracks, artists, genres, decades — all ranked by play count across all sources. Total hours played, total tracks, total albums. Session history. Annual wrap-up — 'your year in music'.

features.desc: Optional Mac app that runs as a menu bar agent on a home Mac. Scans attached drives/NAS. Exposes local library remotely via cloud backend relay. Enables full library access anywhere without VPN or Tailscale. Users without Mac bridge get streaming services fallback when away from home.

features.name: Smart playlists
features.desc: Rules-based auto-generated playlists: genre + decade + unplayed + minimum play count + source combinations. Auto-update as library grows. Similar to iTunes Smart Playlists but cross-source.

features.name: watchOS app
features.desc: Basic playback controls and Now Playing display on Apple Watch. Play/pause/skip/volume. Complications for current track. Scope TBD — deferred until iPhone UI is proven.

features.name: SiriusXM integration
features.desc: Satellite radio via sxm-player library. Subscription required. Legal posture for personal use TBD. Deferred pending decision.

features.name: Scan failure review and targeted rescan utility
features.desc: Settings utility listing permanently failed scans with the specific failure reason for each file, plus a manual rescan action for a selected album. The manual rescan reads a larger block than the standard 64KB tag window. Scoped to a single album so the larger read does not create concurrent session pressure on the NAS. Addresses files whose VORBIS_COMMENT block falls outside the 64KB window because a large embedded PICTURE block precedes it in the FLAC metadata block order — these currently retry five times against identical bytes and fail permanently. RECLASSIFIED 2026-07-27: moved out of fScannerPolish/scanner hardening. The underlying limitation (large embedded PICTURE pushing VORBIS_COMMENT past the 64KB read window) is explicitly staying as a documented, accepted constraint at the parser level, not being fixed here — this is new product surface area (a Settings screen, a list view, a user-triggered rescan action) sitting on top of the scanner, not a correction to something the scanner gets wrong. Every other fScannerPolish item (bDuplicateAlbumDetection, bTagEditsNotDetected, bArtworkSelectionNotBestWins, bAlbumGenreFromFirstTrack) corrects scanner behavior directly; this one doesn't. Standalone feature, own priority/scheduling, not gated on or grouped with scanner work.

features.name: Post-scan reconciliation audit — files attempted vs processed vs DB records
features.desc:
2026-07-28. In-app audit, run after a scan completes, that reconciles two equations which must both balance: (1) files attempted = processed in main pass + resolved via retry + permanently failed; (2) DB record count = processed in main pass + resolved via retry (permanently-failed files correctly produce zero rows per bFailedReadCreatesWrongAlbumFromFallback, excluded by design not accident). Surfaces as a summary screen: Attempted / Processed / Resolved on Retry / Permanently Failed / DB Record Count, with a clear reconciled-or-discrepancy-of-N indicator. Intended location: Library Management (Tom's current lean, not fully decided) or Local Library. Pairs with fScanFailureUtility — this detects something's wrong, that lets the user act on the specific files once known. Also directly supports diagnosing bMissingTracksInAlbum, which is close to the exact tool its own investigation notes call for.

REQUIRES A SCOPING DECISION BEFORE BUILDING, not yet confirmed with Tom in detail: tracks don't currently carry a scan-session identifier, only createdAt/updatedAt timestamps. A time-window heuristic (rows touched between scan start/end) would work for most cases but leaves a real edge case ambiguous — a track updated by this scan that already existed from a prior one. Recommended: add an explicit scanSessionId to Track (and scan_skips), populated by the scanner on every write, so every row is unambiguously attributable to the run that touched it. This is a real, if small, schema addition — worth explicit sign-off before implementation, since the whole point of this feature is catching subtle counting bugs, and its own scoping needs to be unambiguous or a discrepancy becomes uncertain rather than diagnostic.

What already exists vs needs building: files-attempted count and main-pass skip/write-failure counts are already in the scan-start/scan-end log lines. Resolved-via-retry and permanently-failed totals are currently scattered across per-pass retry-scheduler log lines (PASS N COMPLETE), not aggregated into one final running tally — needs building. The DB count check itself is a simple query once the scanSessionId scoping question above is settled.
